metadata.XMP:Description: For the first time in nearly 15 years a Royal Navy fast jet squadron is operating from the flight deck of a Royal Navy aircraft carrier. F-35B Lightnings from the he 809 Naval Air Squadron and the RAFs supporting RAFs Dambusters 617 Squadron joined HMS Prince of Wales in the North Sea for a month of training at the end of September 2024. The fifth-generation jets made the short flight from their base at RAF Marham to the vessel where, over the coming weeks, personnel will learn the art of operating from an aircraft carrier, while others who have been at sea before refresh their skills. The F-35Bs are supported by some 200 engineers, technicians, armourers, logistics and security experts, chefs, meteorologists among others, who joined the 65,000-tonne warship. Commander Nick Smith said it is a milestone moment ahead of a global deployment, Operation High Mast, next year. This is a big moment for 809 Naval Air Squadron, a vital building block to working up with the carrier strike group in preparation for the deployment next year, he explained. To be the commanding officer of a squadron with such a proud heritage is a huge privilege. We are still in our infancy forming as an F-35B squadron, so joining a carrier for the first time is truly a milestone. F-35 pilot Lieutenant Commander Armstrong said that while the Lightning was generations ahead of the Harrier which preceded it, operating it from a carrier remained a challenge. Its a common misconception that everything on an F-35 is automated, he explained. The aircraft will relieve you of a great deal of the workload. Landing is easier, but not easy. Imagine approaching, in the dark, 105ft above the ship, then moving across to set down on the deck. Commander Smith added: The fundamentals of operating F-35B at sea, compared to land  whether you are a pilot or an engineer  are broadly the same. Its just that everything is much more challenging on a ship
metadata.XMP:Headline: Britain Is Back! Royal Navy's Fast Jet Squadron Operates From Their Own Aircraft Carrier For First Time In 15 Years

le-figaro.title: Mort de Théo, 11 ans, à Rennes : sur une berge de la Vilaine, la spirale vengeresse de deux adolescents, mis en examen pour «meurtre»

metadata.IPTC:Caption-Abstract:
On Monday 25 May 2026, the day after the body of a 12-year-old boy who had been strangled (the boy was found with a wet towel tightly wrapped around his neck) was discovered on the banks of the Vilaine in Rennes (France), detectives from the Judicial Police, assisted by a team of divers who searched the river, were looking for clues to shed light on the circumstances of this tragedy.
Lundi 25 mai 2026, au lendemain de la decouverte du corps d un enfant de 12 ans tue par etranglement (le garcon a ete retrouve avec une serviette mouillee fortement serree autour du cou) sur les bords de la Vilaine a Rennes (France), les enqueteurs de la Police Judiciaire epaules par une equipe de plongeurs qui ont sonde la riviere etaient a la recherche d indices afin d eclaircir les circonstances de ce drame. (Photo by Estelle Ruiz / Hans Lucas via AFP)
